lesson_title: The Bakkie That Quietly Gets Cheaper
hook_text: Nothing broke. Nobody crashed it. And it's still worth less every single month.
clip_script: Think of the newest phone in your house. Launch-day price: full and proud. One year later — still working perfectly — try to sell it: maybe two-thirds of the price, maybe less. Nothing broke. Nobody dropped it in the bath. It just... got older, and the world quietly marked it down. Zanele's new bakkie is the same story with bigger numbers: one hundred and fifty thousand rand on the first of March, and from its very first delivery it is worth a little less every month. Should the books keep announcing one hundred and fifty thousand for five straight years? That would be a polite lie — and the books do not lie, not even politely. So the books tell the truth in three numbers: what it cost, what it has lost, and what it is still worth. Receipt, wear, worth.
visual_style: A gleaming bakkie whose price tag ticks downward month by month beside a phone doing the same; three glowing labels — RECEIPT, WEAR, WORTH — snap into place at the close.
pacing: Conversational build to the three-word landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and slice the loss both ways.
